([[Muscatine, Iowa]]) | college = [[Iowa Hawkeyes men's basketball|Iowa]] (2018–2021) | highlights = * Second-team All-[[Big Ten Conference|Big Ten]] ([[2020–21 Big Ten Conference men's basketball season|2021]]) * Third-team All-[[Big Ten Conference|Big Ten]] ([[2019–20 Big Ten Conference men's basketball season#All-Big Ten awards and teams|2020]]) * Big Ten All-Freshman Team (2019) * [[Iowa Mr. Basketball]] (2018) | medal_templates = }} '''Joe Wieskamp''' (born August 23, 1999) is an American [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Iowa Hawkeyes men's basketball|Iowa Hawkeyes]]. ==Early life and high school career== In middle school, Wieskamp played [[American football|football]] as a [[quarterback]] and was a talented [[baseball]] player. He quit football after breaking his thumb and eventually decided to focus solely on basketball.{{cite web |last1=Coss |first1=Matt |title=Going places: Iowa recruit Wieskamp blossoms into elite talent |url=https://qctimes.com/sports/high-school/basketball/boys/going-places-iowa-recruit-wieskamp-blossoms-into-elite-talent/article_04a8e1cc-b90f-5216-8063-2132382587d9.html |website=[[Quad-City Times]] |accessdate=December 16, 2019 |date=December 4, 2016}} Wieskamp played basketball for [[Muscatine High School]] in his hometown of [[Muscatine, Iowa]]. In his freshman season, he averaged 18.6 points per game, which made him the top scoring freshman in Iowa.{{cite web |last1=Cuellar |first1=Chris |title=Meet Joe Wieskamp: Muscatine's young hoops star set to join Hawkeyes in '18 |url=https://www.desmoinesregister.com/story/sports/basketball/2015/07/04/joe-wieskamp-muscatine-high-school-iowa-hawkeyes-basketball/29712349/ |website=[[The Des Moines Register]] |accessdate=December 16, 2019 |date=July 4, 2015}} Wieskamp became the first freshman in [[Mississippi Athletic Conference]] (MAC) history to earn all-conference honors. In his sophomore season, he averaged 21.6 points and 10 rebounds per game and was named first-team all-state. As a junior, Wieskamp averaged 30.4 points and 10.2 rebounds per game and was recognized as MAC Player of the Year. He became the first Iowa Class 4A player to average 30 points since [[Jeff Horner]] in 2002.{{cite web |last1=Lensing |first1=Jeremy |title=Wieskamp named MAC Player of the Year, 1 of 3 Muskies honors |url=https://muscatinejournal.com/sports/high-school/wieskamp-named-mac-player-of-the-year-of-muskies-honors/article_a89c56b2-c742-534b-808e-727189f95869.html |website=[[Muscatine Journal]] |accessdate=December 16, 2019 |date=March 6, 2017}} Wieskamp scored a school-record 50 points in a win over [[Burlington High School (Iowa)|Burlington High School]] to become Muscatine's all-time leading scorer.{{cite web |last1=Bain |first1=Matthew |title=Hawkeye commit scores 50, breaks two school records |url=https://www.hawkcentral.com/story/sports/college/iowa/basketball-men/2016/12/13/hawkeye-commit-joe-wieskamp-scores-50-breaks-two-school-records/95410150/ |website=Hawk Central |accessdate=December 16, 2019 |date=December 13, 2016}} He was voted Iowa [[Gatorade Player of the Year awards|Gatorade Player of the Year]].{{cite web |last1=Goodwin |first1=Cody |title=Meet The Des Moines Register's All-Iowa boys' basketball team |url=https://www.desmoinesregister.com/story/sports/high-school/all-iowa/2017/03/24/all-iowa-boys-basketball-team-2017-des-moines-register/99510888/ |website=[[The Des Moines Register]] |accessdate=December 16, 2019 |date=March 24, 2017}} As a senior, Wieskamp averaged a state-high 33.5 points and 13.5 rebounds per game, leading his team to its first state tournament in 16 years.{{cite web |title=Photos: Joe Wieskamp through the years |url=https://qctimes.com/sports/basketball/college/big-10/iowa/photos-joe-wieskamp-through-the-years/collection_8be0a3ec-0ad5-11ea-8720-ebf2e8c9b790.html |website=[[Quad-City Times]] |accessdate=December 16, 2019 |date=November 21, 2019}} He repeated as Iowa Gatorade Player of the Year and was named [[Iowa Mr. Basketball]]. Wieskamp left high school as the Iowa Class 4A career scoring leader, with 2,376 points.{{cite web |last1=Coss |first1=Matt |title=Muskies' Wieskamp is 2018 Iowa Mr. Basketball |url=https://qctimes.com/sports/high-school/basketball/boys/muskies-wieskamp-is-iowa-mr-basketball/article_a623eb89-7cbc-59bb-a921-4d44d8fcee0c.html |website=[[Quad-City Times]] |accessdate=December 16, 2019 |date=March 13, 2018}} ===Recruiting=== Wieskamp committed to play [[college basketball]] for [[Iowa Hawkeyes men's basketball|Iowa]] on June 9, 2015, before his sophomore year. At the end of his high school career, he was considered a consensus four-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and the best prospect in Iowa. {{College athlete recruit start|40=no|collapse=no|year=2018}} {{College athlete recruit entry | recruit = Joe Wieskamp | position = [[Shooting guard|SG]] | hometown = [[Muscatine, Iowa|Muscatine, IA]] | highschool = [[Muscatine High School|Muscatine]] (IA) | feet = 6 | inches = 6 | weight = 190 | 40 = | commitdate = June 9, 2015 | scout stars = | rivals stars = 4 | 247 stars = 4 | espn stars = 4 | espn grade = 84 }} {{College Athlete Recruit End | 40 = | year = 2018 | rivals ref title = Iowa 2018 Basketball Commitments | scout ref title = | espn ref title = 2018 Iowa Hawkeyes Recruiting Class | 247 ref title = | rivals school = iowa | 247 school = | espn schoolid = 2294 | scout overall = | rivals overall = 43 | 247 overall = 55 | espn overall = 77 | accessdate = May 28, 2020 | bball = yes }} ==College career== [[File:Joe Wieskamp.jpg|thumb|upright|Wieskamp with [[Iowa Hawkeyes men's basketball|Iowa]] in 2019]] On January 20, 2019, Wieskamp went 8-for-8 from the floor and scored a season-high 24 points in a 95–71 win over [[Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball|Illinois]].{{cite web |title=Wieskamp scores 24, No. 23 Iowa routs Illinois 95–71 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401082348 |website=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |accessdate=December 26, 2019 |date=January 20, 2019}} Wieskamp had 19 points and five rebounds against [[Cincinnati Bearcats men's basketball|Cincinnati]] in the NCAA tournament. As a freshman he averaged 11.1 points and 4.9 rebounds per game, shooting 42.4 percent from beyond the arc. He started all 35 games and was named to the [[Big Ten Conference|Big Ten]] All-freshman team. After the season he declared for the [[2019 NBA draft]] but did not hire an agent.{{cite web |url=https://www.thegazette.com/subject/sports/hawkeyes/iowa-mens-basketball/joe-wieskamp-enters-nba-draft-will-he-return-to-iowa-basketball-20190411 |title=Iowa's Joe Wieskamp enters NBA Draft, not hiring agent |website=[[The Gazette (Cedar Rapids)|The Gazette]] |accessdate=December 26, 2019 |date=April 11, 2019}} Wieskamp ultimately decided to withdraw from the draft and return to Iowa.{{cite web |title=University of Iowa's Joe Wieskamp withdraws name from NBA Draft |url=https://www.kcrg.com/content/news/Wieskamp-Withdraws-From-NBA-Draft-510279221.html |website=KCRG |accessdate=December 26, 2019 |date=May 22, 2019}} Coming into his sophomore season, Wieskamp was named to the preseason All-Big Ten team and the watchlist for the Jerry West Award.{{cite web |last=Coss |first=Matt |url=https://qctimes.com/sports/basketball/college/big-10/iowa/wieskamp-ready-to-make-leap-for-hawkeyes/article_ec0d846a-533c-5f48-a778-552bb38f3606.html |website=[[Quad-City Times]] |accessdate=December 26, 2019 |date=October 22, 2019}} In his sophomore season opener, Wieskamp hyperextended his elbow and had a shooting slump to start the season.{{cite web |last1=Emmert |website=Hawk Central |publisher=[[USA Today]] |accessdate=December 26, 2019 |date=November 22, 2019}} On December 9, he had 23 points in a 72–52 win over [[Minnesota Golden Gophers men's basketball|Minnesota]].{{cite web |url=https://www.thegazette.com/subject/sports/hawkeyes/iowa-mens-basketball/iowa-vs-minnesota-basketball-score-recap-joe-wieskamp-20191209 |title=Joe Wieskamp gets Iowa basketball fans buzzed, helps blitz Minnesota |website=[[The Gazette (Cedar Rapids)|The Gazette]] |accessdate=December 26, 2019 |date=December 9, 2019}} Wieskamp scored a then career-high 26 points on January 10, 2020, in a 67–49 win over [[Maryland Terrapins men's basketball|Maryland]].{{cite news |title=Joe Wieskamp with career night as Iowa takes down No. 12 Maryland |url=https://www.kcrg.com/content/sports/Iowa-vs-Maryland-566895751.html |accessdate=January 28, 2020 |work=KCRG |date=January 10, 2020}} He set a new career-high with 30 points on February 8, in a 96–72 win over [[Nebraska Cornhuskers men's basketball|Nebraska]].{{cite news |title=Wieskamp and Garza help No. 17 Iowa rout Nebraska 96–72 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401166213 |accessdate=February 14, 2020 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=February 8, 2020}} At the close of the regular season, Wieskamp was named to the Third Team All-Big Ten by the coaches and media.{{cite press release|url=https://bigten.org/news/2020/3/9/big-ten-unveils-mens-basketball-postseason-honors-on-btn.aspx|title=Big Ten Unveils Men's Basketball Postseason Honors on BTN|publisher=[[Big Ten Conference]] |date=March 9, 2020 |accessdate=March 9, 2020}} He averaged 14.0 points and 6.1 rebounds per game and led the Big Ten in free throw shooting at 85.6 percent.{{cite news |last1=Eickholt |first1=David |title=Joe Wieskamp named third-team all-Big Ten |url=https://247sports.com/college/iowa/Article/Joe-Wieskamp-Iowa-Hawkeyes-All-Big-Ten-Tournament-Fran-McCaffery-NCAA-Bracket-144808027/ |accessdate=April 2, 2020 |work=247 Sports |date=March 9, 2020}} On February 10, 2021, Wieskamp recorded a junior season-high 26 points and 10 rebounds in a 79–66 win against [[Rutgers Scarlet Knights men's basketball|Rutgers]].{{cite web |last1=Emmert |first1=Mark |title=No. 16 Iowa 79, Rutgers 66: Here's what we learned |url=https://www.hawkcentral.com/story/sports/college/iowa/basketball-men/2021/02/10/iowa-basketball-joe-wieskamp-biggest-game-season-no-16-hawkeyes-sweep-rutgers-luka-garza/4410901001/ |website=Hawk Central |access-date=July 28, 2021 |date=February 10, 2021}} As a junior, he averaged 14.8 points and 6.6 rebounds per game, shooting 46 percent from three-point range, and was named to the Second Team All-Big Ten. On April 14, Wieskamp declared for the [[2021 NBA draft]] while maintaining his college eligibility.{{cite web |last1=Kakert |first1=Tom |title=Wieskamp tests NBA Draft process |url=https://iowa.rivals.com/news/wieskamp-tests-nba-draft-process |website=[[Rivals.com|Rivals]] |access-date=July 28, 2021 |date=April 14, 2021}} He later decided to remain in the draft.{{cite web |last1=Fezler |first1=D.
